newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-Italian soccer club Bologna wants London listing.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-Italian soccer club Bologna wants London listing.

text.p: The president of Italian first division soccer club Bologna was quoted on Tuesday as saying that he planned to seek a bourse listing for the club in Britain later this year.
"Its an aim that's very close to my heart," Giuseppe Gazzoni Frascara told the daily Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper.

"Bologna's accounts are good and certified. After the summer we'll go on to the English secondary market where they take into account not just results but also the value of the team. They already have 17 or 18 British clubs quoted there."
He gave no further details of the club's plans.

Bologna were promoted from serie B at the start of the season and are now fifth in the first division, just two points behind second-placed Inter, and chasing a place in European competition. They beat Sampdoria 2-1 at the weekend.
The club is one of several in Italy that have expressed an interest in a bourse listing recently.
Sergio Cragnotti, owner of Lazio and president of Cirio Finanziaria, said last month that his club was determined to be the first in Italy to float.
"I am working to take Lazio on to the bourse as soon as possible, possibly in June, before the summer," he said.
Serie A leaders Juventus last month denied they were about to offer shares to the public.

A flotation in Italy is problematic because most clubs do not meet the disclosure rules applicable on the Milan bourse or requirements for three straight years of profit prior to a listing, share analysts say.
However the Italian government in September opened the way for clubs to list on the stock exchange by passing a decree law allowing them to become profit-making corporations.
Defending champions AC Milan have also been reported to be considering a stock market float.
Managing director Adriano Galliani was quoted last year as saying that the club aimed to float in 1997 and may consider a foreign listing if red tape frustrated its efforts at home.
The club is owned by billionaire media mogul and opposition Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi.
AC Milan's local rivals Internazionale, owned by the oil-rich Moratti family, Napoli and second division Salernitana have also said they are keen to float.
